description: A Director of Workplace Culture must decide whether two employees should resume co-leading a mentoring circle after a disagreement and finalize a temporary facilitation and communication structure that protects participants while preserving the program.

shared_context.S1: Alex and Priya have been co-leading a monthly mentoring circle for employees from several departments.
shared_context.S2: A disagreement during the last session damaged their working relationship, and the next circle is scheduled in four weeks.
shared_context.S3: The mentoring circle currently has 12 participants and is intended to continue rather than be cancelled.
shared_context.S4: The program's standard operating requirements include documenting facilitation arrangements, participant safeguards, and any approved accommodations before the next session's plan is published.
shared_context.S5: Elena's routine planning meetings use a recorded round-robin before a decision: each attendee states any constraint, commitment, or policy point they personally hold that could affect the plan, and the meeting record captures those statements.

PF1.text: Alex signed a repair agreement with Priya after the disagreement stating that they must not co-lead or meet one-to-one for 30 days; communication during that period must go through the program coordinator, with separate weekly check-ins for four weeks. Alex has not sent the agreement to Elena because the repair meeting was arranged by a peer facilitator rather than Elena's office.

PF2.text: Priya has an approved communication accommodation requiring written agendas and discussion prompts at least 2 business days before any live mentoring-circle planning meeting. The accommodation is held by her current manager and was not included in the program materials.

PF3.text: Marcus confirmed in the current HR policy that a mentoring or support group with more than 10 participants must use two facilitators and a documented risk plan whenever one facilitator has been involved in a conduct-related dispute. He has not yet added this interpretation to the program's policy page.

PF4.text: Mira promised Priya and Alex in the repair meeting that she would serve as interim facilitator for the next six weeks if they could not safely co-lead immediately. The promise was made informally and was not included in the calendar proposal.

decisions.interim_facilitator: string; record the primary facilitator name as Mira, with any second-facilitator detail in a separate commitment

acceptance_conditions: Alex and Priya must not resume joint co-leadership immediately.
Mira must be named interim facilitator for exactly six weeks.
Planning materials must be provided at least 2 business days before live planning meetings.
Separate weekly check-ins must be scheduled for exactly four weeks during the repair period.
The two-facilitator requirement must be explicitly confirmed.
A documented risk plan must be completed.
The settlement must include a commitment for the separate check-ins.
The settlement must include a commitment for the documented risk plan.

content_checks.C2: decisions['interim_facilitator'] == 'Mira' or decisions['interim_facilitator'] == 'Mira (one of two required facilitators; second facilitator to be confirmed)' or decisions['interim_facilitator'] == 'Mira (plus one additional co-facilitator to be identified)'

decisive_facts.why: The 30-day no-co-lead and no-one-to-one agreement changes joint co-leadership to prohibited, requires separate weekly check-ins, and fixes their duration at exactly four weeks.
Priya's accommodation changes the planning process from an unspecified notice period to exactly 2 business days for written agendas and prompts.
The policy's more-than-10-participant threshold combined with a conduct dispute changes the structure to require two facilitators and an explicitly documented risk plan.
Mira's prior promise changes the interim staffing choice to Mira and fixes the temporary arrangement at exactly six weeks.
